We have mass spec: m/z 193.1103 (most intense). Likely molecular ion M+? So molecular weight ~193.11. Proton NMR shows signals: 1.20 (d, 3H) typical methyl attached to CH (ethyl). 2.85 (d, 2H) maybe CH2 next to carbonyl? 3.09 (qdd, 1H) maybe CH attached to CH3 and CH2? 3.81 (s, 3H) methoxy. Aromatic: 7.15 (ddd, 2H) and 7.92 (ddd, 2H) typical para-disubstituted aromatic? Two sets of doublets? Actually ddd suggests ortho meta para couplings. Could be anisole ring (methoxy) with para substituent? The aromatic pattern of 2H each suggests para-disubstituted benzene. So ring has two substituents: one methoxy (OCH3) and something else (maybe carbonyl chain). The chain: maybe -CO-CH2-CH(CH3)-OH? Let's compute formula.

Proposed SMILES from validation: "COc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)CC(C)O". That's anisic acid derivative? Actually anisole (methoxy phenyl) attached to carbonyl (C=O) then CH2-CH(CH3)-OH (hydroxypropyl). Let's compute molecular weight.

We can get formula via get_formula_from_smiles.
